SOURCE: Rand, McNally & Co.'s Indexed Pocket Map and Shippers' Guide of Quebec (Chicago, 1911).
        Internet Archive item randmcnallycosin00rand. NOT lending-restricted; full djvu text
        downloaded and searched 2026-09-06. "Kanawana" occurs exactly once, at line 3461.

HOW TO READ THE KANAWANA LINE. It carries a county and one parenthesis: "Kanawana, Terrebonne,
  (Summer P. O.)". It has NO map grid reference, NO railway number, NO population figure and
  NONE of the reference marks. Compare Kamouraska immediately above it -- "Kamouraska, E-18 * t
  600" -- which carries a grid square, a money-order post office mark, a telegraph station mark
  and a population of 600.

WHAT IT ESTABLISHES: that a summer post office called Kanawana existed in Terrebonne county in
  1911, one year after the YMCA bought the Saint-Sauveur site. The Universal Postal Union's
  supplement of 1912 brackets its opening to between March 1909 and June 1912; this narrows the
  closing end of that bracket to 1911. It also puts "summer" on the office EIGHT YEARS earlier
  than the Sessional Papers of 1919, which was this project's first evidence of it.

NOT ESTABLISHED, and not inferred: why the entry has no grid reference. Some entries in this
  index lack one and some do not, and no rule for it was found in the front matter.
